en: Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Bakr—meaning Ibn Mudar—narrated to us, from Ibn al-Had, that Ziyad ibn Abi Ziyad, the client of Ibn 'Ayyash, narrated to him from 'Irak ibn Malik: I heard him narrating to 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz from 'A'ishah, that she said: A poor woman came to me carrying two daughters of hers, so I gave her three dates to eat. She gave each of them a date, and raised a date to her mouth to eat it, but her two daughters asked her for food. So she split the date that she had wanted to eat between them. Her deed impressed me, and I mentioned what she had done to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). He said: "Indeed, Allah has decreed Paradise for her because of it, or has emancipated her from the Fire because of it."

Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Quhzadh narrated to us: Salamah ibn Sulayman narrated to us: 'Abdullah informed us: Ma'mar informed us, from Ibn Shihab: 'Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Hazm narrated to me, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah; (H) and 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Bahram and Abu Bakr ibn Ishaq narrated to me—and the wording is theirs—they said: Abu al-Yaman informed us: Shu'ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri: 'Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr narrated to me that 'Urwah informed him that 'A'ishah, the wife of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), said: A woman came to me accompanied by two daughters of hers, begging of me, and she did not find anything with me except a single date. So I gave it to her, and she took it and divided it between her two daughters, not eating any of it herself. Then she stood up and left with her two daughters. The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) entered upon me, and I told him her story. The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Whoever is tested with any of these daughters and treats them well, they will be a shield for him against the Fire."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from Burayd ibn 'Abdillah, from his grandfather, from Abu Musa, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace); (H) and Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' al-Hamdani narrated to us—and the wording is his: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Burayd, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "The example of a righteous companion and an evil companion is like that of a musk seller and a blacksmith's bellows. As for the musk seller, he may either give you some as a gift, or you may buy from him, or you may find a pleasant scent from him. And as for the blacksmith's bellows, he may either burn your clothes, or you may find a foul odor."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: 'Ali ibn Mushir and Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, from Burayd ibn 'Abdillah, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, who said: Whenever a person seeking a need came to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), he would turn to those sitting with him and say: "Intercede, and you will be rewarded; and let Allah decree through the tongue of His Prophet whatever He pleases."

Abu Ghassan al-Misma'i narrated to me: 'Uthman ibn 'Umar narrated to us: Abu 'Amir—meaning al-Khazzaz—narrated to us, from Abu 'Imran al-Jawni, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Samit, from Abu Dharr, who said: The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to me: "Do not belittle any good deed, even meeting your brother with a cheerful face."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Ibn Idris narrated to us: Shu'bah informed us; (H) and Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Ibn Idris narrated to us: Shu'bah informed us, from Abu 'Imran al-Jawni, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Samit, from Abu Dharr, who said: Indeed, my close friend (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) advised me: "When you cook a broth, add more water to it, then look to a household among your neighbors and serve them from it with kindness."

Abu Kamil al-Jahdari and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us—and the wording is Ishaq's; Abu Kamil said: "narrated to us," and Ishaq said: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Abd al-Samad al-'Ammi informed us: Abu 'Imran al-Jawni narrated to us, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Samit, from Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "O Abu Dharr, when you cook a broth, add more water to it and look after your neighbors."

'Ubaydullah ibn 'Umar al-Qawariri narrated to me: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, from 'Umar ibn Muhammad, from his father, who said: I heard Ibn 'Umar say: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Gabriel kept enjoining good treatment of the neighbor upon me until I thought he would make him an heir."

'Amr al-Naqid narrated to me: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Abi Hazim narrated to us: Hisham ibn 'Urwah narrated to me, from his father, from 'A'ishah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), the like of it.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Malik ibn Anas; (H) and Qutaybah and Muhammad ibn Rumh narrated to us, from al-Layth ibn Sa'd; (H) and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: 'Abdah and Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us—all of them from Yahya ibn Sa'id; (H) and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us—and the wording is his: 'Abd al-Wahhab—meaning al-Thaqafi—narrated to us: I heard Yahya ibn Sa'id: Abu Bakr—who is Ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn Hazm—informed me that 'Amrah narrated to him that she heard 'A'ishah say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: "Gabriel kept enjoining good treatment of the neighbor upon me until I thought he would surely make him an heir."

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Yazid ibn Zuray' informed us, from Rawh ibn al-Qasim; (H) and Ahmad ibn 'Uthman ibn Hakim narrated to me: Khalid ibn Makhlad narrated to us, from Sulayman ibn Bilal—all of them from Suhayl, with this chain of transmission, the like of it.

'Abdullah ibn Maslamah ibn Qa'nab narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said; (H) and Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: I read to Malik, from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "When a man says, 'The people are ruined,' he is the most ruined among them (or: he has ruined them)." Abu Ishaq said: I do not know whether it is "ahlakahum" (in the accusative: he ruined them) or "ahlakuhum" (in the nominative: he is the most ruined of them).

Suwayd ibn Sa'id narrated to me: Hafs ibn Maysarah narrated to me, from al-'Ala' ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Many a disheveled person turned away at the doors, if he were to swear an oath by Allah, Allah would fulfill it."

Suwayd ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman, from his father: Abu 'Imran al-Jawni narrated to us, from Jundab, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) narrated: "A man said: 'By Allah, Allah will not forgive so-and-so!' Whereupon Allah, the Exalted, said: 'Who is the one swearing by Me that I will not forgive so-and-so? Indeed, I have forgiven so-and-so and made your deeds void'—or as he said."

Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Azdi narrated to us: 'Umar ibn Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us: my father narrated to us: al-A'mash narrated to us: Abu Ishaq narrated to us, from Abu Muslim al-Agharr, that he narrated to him from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri and Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "[Allah says:] 'Might is My lower garment and pride is My cloak; whoever contests with Me for either of them, I will punish him.'"

Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)—so he mentioned several hadiths, among which was: And the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "A woman entered the Fire because of a cat of hers—or a tomcat—which she tied up, neither feeding it nor letting it loose to forage from the vermin of the earth, until it died of emaciation."

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Abu Bakr ibn Shu'ayb ibn al-Habhab informed us, from Abu al-Wazi' al-Rasibi, from Abu Barzah al-Aslami, that Abu Barzah said: I said to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace): "O Messenger of Allah, I do not know, perhaps you will pass away while I remain after you, so grant me some provision (of beneficial knowledge) by which Allah will benefit me." The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Do such-and-such, do such-and-such"—Abu Bakr forgot it—"and remove harm from the path."

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Aban ibn Sam'ah: Abu al-Wazi' narrated to me: Abu Barzah narrated to me, saying: I said: "O Prophet of Allah, teach me something by which I may benefit." He said: "Remove harm from the pathway of the Muslims."

Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)—so he mentioned several hadiths, among which was: And the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "None of you should point a weapon at his brother, for none of you knows, perhaps Satan may cause his hand to strike, and thus he falls into a pit of the Fire."
Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, from Ibn 'Awn, from Muhammad, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), the like of it.

'Amr al-Naqid and Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to me—'Amr said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Ibn Sirin: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: Abu al-Qasim (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Whoever points a piece of iron at his brother, indeed the angels curse him, even if he were his full brother through his father and mother."

'Abdullah ibn Barrad al-Ash'ari and Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' narrated to us—and the wording is 'Abdullah's—they said: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Burayd, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "When one of you passes through our mosque or our marketplace carrying arrows, let him hold their tips with his palm lest he inflict something on any of the Muslims with them," or he said: "let him grasp their tips."

Haddab ibn Khalid narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "When one of you passes through an assembly or a marketplace with arrows in his hand, let him grasp their tips, then let him grasp their tips, then let him grasp their tips." He said: Abu Musa said: "By Allah, we did not die before we ended up aiming them at one another's faces!"

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn Rumh narrated to us: al-Layth informed us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), that he commanded a man who was giving arrows as charity in the mosque not to pass with them except while holding their tips. And Ibn Rumh said: "he was giving arrows as charity (yassaddaqu)."

Yahya ibn Yahya and Abu al-Rabi' narrated to us—Abu al-Rabi' said: "narrated to us," and Yahya said—and the wording is his: Hammad ibn Zayd informed us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Jabir ibn 'Abdillah, that a man passed through the mosque with arrows whose tips were exposed, so he was commanded to hold their tips so that he would not scratch any Muslim.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us—Ishaq said: "informed us," and Abu Bakr said: "narrated to us": Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from 'Amr: he heard Jabir say: A man passed through the mosque with arrows, so the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to him: "Hold their tips."

Abu al-Tahir narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, that Hisham ibn Hakim found a man—while he was governor of Hims—detaining people of the Nabataeans in the sun regarding payment of the jizyah. So he said: "What is this? Indeed, I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: 'Indeed, Allah will punish those who torment people in this world.'"

Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Waki' and Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us; (H) and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Jarir informed us—all of them from Hisham, with this chain of transmission. And in the hadith of Jarir he added: He said: and their governor that day over Palestine was 'Umayr ibn Sa'd; so he went in to him and narrated it to him, whereupon he ordered them to be released.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, who said: Hisham ibn Hakim ibn Hizam passed by some Nabataean people in the Levant who had been made to stand in the sun. He asked: "What is the matter with them?" They said: "They have been detained regarding the jizyah." So Hisham said: "I testify that I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: 'Indeed, Allah will punish those who torment people in this world.'"

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from Hisham ibn Hakim ibn Hizam, who said: He passed by some people in the Levant who had been made to stand in the sun and oil had been poured over their heads. He asked: "What is this?" It was said: "They are being punished regarding the land-tax (al-kharaj)." So he said: "As for me, I certainly heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: 'Indeed, Allah will punish those who torment people in this world.'"
